title: Cross-pool Credit Allocator and SLA Tradeoffs
body:
Purpose
——
Working spreadsheet-style doc capturing a proposal for a cross-pool credit allocator: a lightweight accounting layer that lets Dedicated customers trade (or use) unused commit capacity across GPU pools with defined SLA tradeoffs and amortization. Goal is to reduce idle-sink write-offs while keeping commitments predictable from a revenue and ops perspective.

Context and motivation
——
- Observed: multi-tenant customers and internal product teams underutilize reserved pools due to skewed load windows (e.g., development daytime vs. production nighttime).
- Problem: idle reserved GPUs create sunk cost; discounting/credits today is coarse (one-off credits or manual negotiation).
- Opportunity: create an automated credit allocator that: (a) preserves committed revenue baseline, (b) surfaces predictable discounts via credits for customers that agree to flexible SLAs, and (c) permits internal cross-pool backfills.

Definitions (short)
——
- Commit-hour: 1 GPU-hour reserved under a paid commit.
- Credit-hour: a tradable unit representing a portion of commit-hour made available from an underutilized pool (e.g., 0.25 GPU-hour increments).
- Swap window: time range where credit-hours can be used by other pools (e.g., 00:00–06:00 PT).
- SLA-tier: latency/availability expectation attached to usage (Gold / Silver / Bronze).
- Amortization factor: fraction of monthly commit revenue we attribute per credit-hour when calculating ledger balances.

Baseline assumptions for model
——
- Example customer commit: 100 reserved A100-hours/day at $X/hour effective rate.
- Average actual utilization observed: 65% (weekday variance ±20%).
- Expected burstable demand: 10% of pool capacity can safely be exposed as credits without risking full-commit contention if we enforce per-minute headroom.
- Credit granularity: 0.25 GPU-hour (15m) to minimize bookkeeping and keep scheduling simple.

Allocation rules (proposal)
——
1) Daily reconciliation window (00:00–02:00 PT): pools report unused commit-hours from previous day (rounded down to nearest credit granule).
2) Internal priority: first attempt internal same-organization backfill (cross-team), then external marketplace (if customer opted-in).
3) SLA mapping: credit consumption binds to a SLA-tier. Credits consumed under Bronze receive deeper amortized discount but lower preemption protections.
4) Preemption: credit-backed jobs are preemptible with N-second eviction notice (configurable by SLA).
5) Caps: per-customer cap on credits borrowed = min(20% of their committed capacity, fixed X credits) to avoid runaway usage.

Simple accounting ledger (spreadsheet rows)
——
- Columns: date | pool_id | committed_hours | used_hours | unused_hours | credits_generated | credits_consumed_internal | credits_consumed_external | amortized_credit_value | net_revenue_impact
- Sample row (text formatting):
  2024-09-17 | pool-A | 2400 | 1560 | 840 | 840 / 0.25 = 3360 credits | 1200 | 960 | $0.12/credit | $-1,036

Scenario matrix (sensitivity slices)
——
- Vary utilization baseline: 60%, 70%, 80%
- Vary opt-in rate: 30%, 60%, 90% of customers allow external credit exposure
- Vary amortization fraction: 5%, 10%, 20% of monthly revenue attributable to credits
- Vary credit price discount vs commit: 20%, 40%, 60% (Bronze deeper discount)

Mini table (expected outcomes):
  Scenario | Util | Opt-in | Amort% | Revenue delta | Idle write-off delta
  S1 | 60% | 30% | 10% | -3.8% | -18%
  S2 | 70% | 60% | 10% | -1.1% | -44%
  S3 | 80% | 90% | 5%  | +0.5% | -62%

Operational knobs and safety nets
——
- Min headroom threshold: don’t expose credits if pool utilization in last 24h > 85%.
- Conservative cooldown: newly created credits from a pool cannot be consumed externally for 12h to avoid oscillation.
- Emergency hold: an operator can place a 24h hold per pool preventing credit generation (manual override).

SLA tradeoffs and customer UX language (draft bullets)
——
- Bronze credits: up to 60% discount to commit rate, preemptible, best-effort regional routing. Recommended for batch inference and non-latency-critical tasks.
- Silver credits: up to 35% discount, preemptible with longer grace, regional guaranteed availability windows.
- Gold credits: small discount (10–15%), near-nonpreemptible, limited to internal cross-team only (not external marketplace).
- UX: customers see an "Available Credits" ledger in Console per-pool with a forecasted hourly burn estimate. Opt-in is explicit per-pool and reversible with a 7-day cooling-off for revenue accounting.

Pricing and revenue model implications (notes)
——
- Conservative approach aims to be revenue-neutral at 70% utilization and 50% opt-in: we price credits so that amortized discount + increased fill rate ≈ base revenue.
- Upside: higher reported utilization improves IRR on reserved purchases, enabling more aggressive committed pricing for future cohorts.
- Downside: poorly tuned discounts can create cannibalization — customers may shift workloads to cheaper credits rather than increase commit levels. Caps and SLA differentiation mitigate this.

Open questions to model in spreadsheet
——
- How to split amortization across months when credits originate mid-month? (front-load vs pro-rata)
- Should credits have expiry? (30/60/90 day experiment)
- How to account for GPU-type heterogeneity (A100 vs H100) in credit pricing and granularity?

Recommended default parameters for the pilot (numbers for the spreadsheet)
——
- Credit granularity: 0.25 GPU-hour
- Min headroom: 15% (do not generate credits if average utilization >85%)
- Opt-in default: internal-only (external marketplace opt-in must be explicit)
- Amortization fraction for pilot: 10% of monthly commit revenue allocated to credits ledger
- CPI (credit price index) baseline: Bronze 40% of commit rate, Silver 70% of commit rate, Gold 90% of commit rate
- Cap on borrow: 20% of borrower’s committed capacity per 24h

Next steps / action items
——
- Product: build a minimal ledger schema in a sheet and wire sample pool CSVs (owner: Maya, due: 2024-09-30).
- Eng infra: estimate schedule complexity to enforce per-minute headroom and eviction signals (owner: Evan, due: 2024-10-07).
- Finance: run P&L sensitivity across the three scenario slices and assess monthly cashflow timing (owner: Ravi, due: 2024-10-10).
- Legal: review customer-facing opt-in language and revenue recognition implications (owner: Sophie, due: 2024-10-15).

Appendix: example computational notes (plain text)
——
- credits_generated = floor(unused_hours / 0.25)
- amortized_credit_value = (monthly_commit_revenue * amortization_fraction) / total_credits_issued_this_month
- sample: monthly_commit_revenue = $72,000, amort_fraction = 0.1 => pool-of-credit-value = $7,200. If total_credits_issued=60,000 => $0.12/credit.

Notes to reviewers
——
- This is intentionally conservative in the pilot: favor operational simplicity and protection of committed revenue. The sheet will include per-pool sample data, a simulator tab for 90-day rolling demand traces, and a payouts tab showing ledger settlements.
- Looking for feedback specifically on: credit expiry length, cap sizes, and amortization granularity (daily vs monthly).

End of doc
